# Billing Migration Error Codes and Fixes This article lists the error codes that can appear while a billing profile is
being migrated to the new billing platform, what each code means, and the
recommended fix. | Error code | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| ERR-4032 | Billing profile migration is incomplete because a required field was not carried over from the legacy platform | Reconnect the billing profile and retry the migration from the Billing Overview page |
| ERR-4040 | The legacy payment method on file could not be re-verified with the card network | Add a new payment method and set it as default before retrying migration |
| ERR-4155 | Migration was queued but a duplicate billing profile already exists for this account | Contact billing support to merge the duplicate profile before retrying |
| ERR-5010 | The invoice account is locked because of a prior unresolved dispute | Ask an account administrator to resolve the dispute, then unlock the invoice account |
| ERR-5020 | Tax identification data could not be transferred because it was stored in an unsupported legacy format | Re-enter tax identification information manually on the new billing platform | ## How to Read This Table

This table summarizes the ranges used across all error series to help you
quickly identify the category of an error code you are seeing. | Range | Series | Category | Typical blocking behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| ERR-4xxx | Core migration | Profile and data field errors | Blocking |
| ERR-5xxx | Core migration | Account state restrictions | Non-blocking (restricted state) |
| PAY-1xxx | Payment | Payment method errors | Blocking |
| INV-2xxx | Invoice | Invoice history and configuration | Mixed |
| TAX-3xxx | Tax | Tax identity and configuration | Mixed |
| SUB-4xxx | Subscription | Plan and entitlement mapping | Mixed |
| ACC-5xxx | Account | Profile and ownership | Mixed |
| DAT-6xxx | Data integrity | Checksum and record validation | Blocking |
| NET-7xxx | Network | Connectivity and timeouts | Non-blocking (transient) |
| ROLE-8xxx | Roles | Permission and role mapping | Non-blocking |
| SYNC-9xxx | Sync | Integration synchronization | Non-blocking | ## Escalation Decision Tree

**Can multiple error codes appear at the same time?**
Yes. A single migration attempt can surface multiple error codes if several
conditions are unmet simultaneously. All blocking errors must be resolved
before migration can proceed. You do not need to resolve non-blocking errors
before retrying — they will be re-evaluated as migration progresses. **Will I lose data if migration fails?**
No. Migration is transactional. If a failure occurs during the in progress
phase, the migration engine rolls back any partial writes to the new platform. The legacy platform remains unchanged and authoritative until migration
successfully completes. **Is there an error code for "too many retries"?**
Not directly. However, if the migration engine detects that an account has
retried more than 5 times in a 24-hour window without a change in account
state, it enters a "manual review required" state. You will receive an email
and a support ticket is automatically opened on your behalf. **My error code is not in this article. What should I do?**
Error codes not listed here are internal diagnostic codes generated by the
migration engine infrastructure. They are not intended to be acted on by
account administrators. Contact billing support with the exact error code,
and a support engineer will interpret the code and provide remediation
instructions. **Can I prevent error codes from appearing?**
Most error codes can be avoided by completing the Pre-Migration Checklist in
the "Billing Profile Migration Overview" article before migration begins. Completing the checklist resolves the conditions that cause the most common
blocking errors (ERR-4032, PAY-1001, PAY-1004, INV-2003, TAX-3002). **How long do non-blocking error codes stay on my account?**
Non-blocking error codes remain visible on the migration status page until the
underlying condition is resolved. Once resolved, the error is marked as
"resolved" and archived in the migration event log. Archived errors remain
visible in the migration history for 12 months for audit purposes.

or retrieve the current error code programmatically, use these endpoints. ### Check Migration Status ```
GET /v2/accounts/{account_id}/migration/status Response:
{
  "migration_id": "mig_01HVXK3QZ...",
  "status": "queued" | "in_progress" | "completed" | "failed",
  "error_code": "ERR-4032" | null,
  "error_message": "...",
  "queued_at": "2026-06-01T08:00:00Z",
  "started_at": "2026-06-01T09:00:00Z" | null,
  "completed_at": null,
  "retry_count": 0
}
``` ### Trigger a Retry ```
POST /v2/accounts/{account_id}/migration/retry Response:
{
  "migration_id": "mig_01HVXK3QZ...",
  "status": "queued",
  "retry_count": 1
}
``` Retries are rate-limited to 1 per hour per account. If you attempt a retry

response with a `Retry-After` header indicating the number of seconds until
the next retry is allowed. ### List All Error Codes for an Account ```

# Migration Rollback and Support Escalation ## When a Rollback Is Possible A billing profile migration can be rolled back to the legacy platform only if
the migration has not yet reached the **completed** stage. Once a migration
reaches completed status, it cannot be rolled back, because invoice numbering
and tax records have already switched to the new platform's format. ## Rollback-Related Error Codes | Error code | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| ERR-6001 | Rollback was requested after the migration already reached completed status | Rollback is not available; contact billing support for a manual correction instead |
| ERR-6015 | Rollback failed because the legacy billing profile was already archived | Contact billing support to restore the archived legacy profile before retrying rollback |
| ERR-6030 | Rollback was requested by a user without the Billing Administrator role | Ask an Account Owner or Billing Administrator to submit the rollback request | ## How to Request a Rollback Go to the Billing Overview page. Select "Request rollback" under Migration Status. Provide a reason for the rollback request. Rollback requests are processed within 4 business hours while migration is
still in the queued or in-progress stage. ## Escalating to Support

**Will migration affect my current subscription or pricing?**
No. Subscription terms, pricing, seat counts, and renewal dates are preserved
exactly. Migration is a platform transfer, not a contract change. **Do I need to re-enter my payment information?**
Most payment methods are migrated automatically. You may be asked to re-verify
a payment method if the token exchange cannot be confirmed during migration. A
re-verification prompt will appear on the Billing Overview page. **Will my invoice number reset after migration?**
No. Invoice numbers continue from where the legacy platform left off. If your
last legacy invoice was INV-2024-08742, your next invoice will be
INV-2024-08743. **What happens if I receive an invoice during the migration window?**
Invoices generated during the in progress phase are deferred. Payment is
collected automatically within 24 hours of migration completing. A 7-day
grace period applies; late fees are not charged during this window. **Can I opt out of migration?**
No. Migration to the new billing platform is mandatory for all accounts. However, the timing of your migration window can be adjusted in limited
circumstances. Contact billing support at least 14 days before your scheduled
window to request a reschedule. **What happens to my tax exemption certificates?**
Approved certificates are migrated. If a certificate expires within 30 days
of your migration date, you will receive a renewal prompt. Billing continues
to apply the exemption until the certificate expires. **How do I know when migration is complete?**
You will receive an email to all billing contacts when migration completes. A
green confirmation banner also appears on the Billing Overview page. **Can migration be reversed after it completes?**
No. Once migration reaches completed status, it cannot be rolled back. Invoice numbering and tax records have already switched to the new platform's
format, and reversing them would create compliance issues. **Why does my Billing Overview page show incomplete data during migration?**
The Billing Overview page reads from the new platform as soon as migration
starts. While data is still being transferred, some fields may show as empty
or stale. This is expected. The page returns to normal once migration completes. **Are there any downtime windows during migration?**
No planned downtime. Write operations to billing endpoints are blocked during
the in progress phase (returning 503 responses), but the platform remains
accessible and all read operations are available. **What if I update my payment method right before migration starts?**
Updates made less than 1 hour before the in progress phase may not be captured
before the profile snapshot is taken. If you need to update a payment method,
do so at least 2 hours before your scheduled migration window. **How do multi-account organizations handle a failure in one child account?**
A failure in one child account does not block other child accounts or the
primary account from completing migration. The failed child account retries
independently once the error is resolved. **Will my API keys stop working immediately after migration?**
Legacy API keys continue to work against the legacy API endpoint for 90 days
after migration. After 90 days, the legacy endpoint is retired and only new
API keys on the new endpoint will work. **Can I generate a new invoice manually during migration?**
No. Manual invoice generation is blocked during the in progress phase. Once
migration completes, you can generate invoices normally. **Does migration affect my SSO login?**
No. SSO configuration is managed by the identity platform, which is separate
from billing. Login is not affected. **What is the difference between a queued and a stuck migration?**
Queued is the normal waiting state before migration begins. Stuck is an
informal term for a migration that has been in queued status for longer than
expected — usually because a prerequisite is not met. If your migration has
been queued for more than 24 hours, check the Billing Overview page for a
yellow "Action required" banner. **Do I need to do anything for my recurring billing after migration?**
Auto-pay resumes automatically after migration. No action is required unless
the account owner is prompted to confirm the default payment method. **Will I lose my promotional discount after migration?**
No. Promotional pricing, including grandfathered legacy pricing, is preserved
through migration. **How are invoice PDFs handled after the legacy portal is decommissioned?**
All invoice PDFs, including those generated on the legacy platform, are
accessible from the new platform's invoice list. The legacy portal remains
available for 90 days as a backup access method. **What should I do if I see a billing discrepancy after migration?**
Submit a billing dispute from Billing > Invoices > [Invoice] > Dispute. Include
the invoice number and a description of the discrepancy. The billing support
team will investigate and respond within 5 business days. **Account Owner:** The user with the highest privilege level on a billing
account. Responsible for confirming migration and is the primary recipient of
billing notifications. **ACH:** Automated Clearing House. A US-based electronic bank transfer network
used for direct debit payment methods. **Billing Administrator:** A secondary role with full billing access. Can
perform all billing operations except modify the Account Owner role. **Billing Contact:** Any user with a billing role on the account who receives
billing notifications. **Chargeback:** A payment reversal initiated by the card issuer at the
cardholder's request. Opens a dispute on the billing account. **Credit:** A positive balance applied to an account that reduces the amount
charged on the next invoice. **Entitlement:** A feature or resource limit granted by a subscription plan. **Finance Viewer:** A read-only billing role. Can view invoices and payment

customers but is retained for existing subscribers who subscribed before the
plan was discontinued. **Invoice:** A document requesting payment for services rendered, generated
at the end of each billing cycle. **Legacy Platform:** The previous billing infrastructure that accounts are
migrating away from. **Migration Window:** The scheduled time period during which an account's
billing data is transferred from the legacy platform to the new platform. **New Platform:** The current billing infrastructure that all accounts are
migrating to. **Plan ID:** A unique identifier for a subscription plan. Changes from legacy
format to new format during migration. **PO (Purchase Order):** A payment method used by businesses to pay invoices

storing the actual card or bank details. **TIN (Tax Identification Number):** A number assigned by a tax authority to

endpoint when a billing event occurs.

**What if I miss my migration window?**
If you do not complete any required actions before your migration window, the
window is extended automatically. Migration will not proceed to the in
progress phase until all blocking prerequisites are met. There is no penalty
for missing the original window. **Can I have two active subscriptions after migration?**
Yes. Migration does not change the number of active subscriptions on the
account. If you had two active subscriptions before migration, you will have
two after. **What happens to my billing address if I have multiple addresses on file?**
The default billing address is migrated and remains the default. All
additional addresses are also migrated. The default address selection does not
change. **How are refunds handled during migration?**
Pending refunds initiated before migration are processed on the legacy platform
before the migration window begins. Refunds requested during the migration
window are queued and processed on the new platform after migration completes. **Is there a way to test migration in a staging environment?**
Yes. If your account has a linked staging or sandbox environment, a test
migration is automatically run against the staging environment 48 hours before
the production migration window. The test migration uses production data
snapshots to validate the migration process. Results of the test migration are
emailed to billing contacts. **Will my usage data and analytics reset after migration?**
No. Usage data and analytics are stored in a separate analytics system that
is not part of the billing profile migration. Your usage history is unaffected. **Can I change the account owner before migration?**
Yes, but it is strongly recommended to complete the account owner change at
least 72 hours before the migration window to ensure the new owner's email
is verified and the change is reflected in the billing profile before migration
is scheduled. **What if I discover a discrepancy in my invoice history after migration?**
Submit a billing dispute from Billing > Invoices > [Invoice] > Dispute. The
billing support team will compare the new platform's records with the legacy
platform's records (the legacy platform remains in read-only mode for 90 days
after migration) and resolve any discrepancy. **Do I need to update my accounts payable system after migration?**
If your accounts payable system stores the billing platform's API base URL
or invoice portal URL, update these references after migration. Invoice
numbers and amounts will not change, so existing records in your AP system
remain accurate. **What is the migration engine?**
The migration engine is the internal service that reads billing data from the
legacy platform and writes it to the new platform. It runs as a managed
service inside the billing platform infrastructure and is not directly
accessible to account administrators or support agents. **How many accounts are migrated simultaneously?**
The migration engine runs up to 500 accounts in parallel during a migration
window. Accounts are batched by size to prevent large accounts from blocking
the queue. Enterprise and Government accounts are migrated in dedicated batches
outside of the shared migration window. **Can I pause migration once it has started?**
Migration cannot be paused once the in progress phase has begun. If you need
to stop migration, wait until it either completes or fails. If it fails, it
automatically reverts to queued status and no further action is taken until
you retry. **What if my company name changes during the migration window?**
If your registered business name changes during the migration window, wait
until migration completes before updating the name. Updating account details
during the in progress phase may cause a data consistency error. **Are there any file size limits on tax exemption certificates?**
Yes. The new platform accepts PDF files up to 10 MB. Files larger than 10 MB
must be compressed or split before uploading. **What credit card networks are supported on the new platform?**
Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, Diners Club, UnionPay, and JCB
are all supported. The legacy platform did not support UnionPay or JCB; if
your account has a UnionPay or JCB card on file, it will be migrated and will
become active on the new platform for the first time. **Can I use the legacy platform to generate reports after migration?**
The legacy platform is in read-only mode for 90 days after migration. You can
view and export data from the legacy platform's reporting module during this
period. After 90 days, the legacy platform is decommissioned and reporting
is only available from the new platform. **What happens to scheduled subscription renewals that fall during the
migration window?**
Subscription renewals that fall during the in progress phase are deferred and
processed automatically on the new platform within 4 hours of migration
completing. You will receive a renewal invoice shortly after migration
completes if a renewal was deferred. **Can billing contacts receive migration status updates via SMS?**
SMS notifications for migration status are not currently available. Email
is the only notification channel for migration status updates. In-app banners
on the Billing Overview page also display real-time status. **What should I do if a billing contact's email address changed just before
migration?**
Update the email address in Billing > Contacts at least 24 hours before the
migration window. Email changes take up to 24 hours to propagate. If the
migration window starts before the update propagates, the old address will
receive migration notifications. **Are there any differences in invoice formatting between the legacy and new
platforms?**
The default invoice layout is updated on the new platform. The key changes
are: company logo placement has moved from the top right to the top left;
the invoice due date is now displayed more prominently; line item descriptions
support up to 500 characters (up from 255 on the legacy platform); and a QR
code linking to the online payment portal is included by default. **Can I use a different currency for different subscriptions after migration?**
Yes. The new platform supports per-subscription currency assignment for
Business and Enterprise accounts. Contact billing support to configure
multi-currency subscriptions after migration. **What is the maximum number of payment methods I can have on my account?**
The new platform supports up to 25 payment methods per account (up from 10
on the legacy platform). All payment methods from the legacy platform will
be migrated regardless of this limit; the limit applies only to methods added
after migration. **Will the migration affect my NetSuite or QuickBooks integration?**
If you use an accounting integration (NetSuite, QuickBooks, Xero, or similar),
the integration will need to be re-authenticated after migration because the
billing account ID format changes. You may also see a SYNC-9001 or SYNC-9002
error code. See the integration-specific reconnection guide in Billing >
Integrations > [Integration name] > Reconnect. ## Appendix C: Migration Error Code Quick Reference | Code | Series | Blocking | One-line description |

# Billing Profile Migration — Complete Implementation Guide ## What Is Billing Profile Migration? Billing profile migration moves your billing profile — payment methods, invoice
history, tax information, and subscription entitlements — from the legacy
billing platform to the new billing platform. Migration happens automatically
for most accounts, but some accounts require the account owner to confirm the
migration before it completes. Migration runs in three stages: **queued**, **in progress**, and
**completed**. You can check your current stage on the Billing Overview page
under Account Settings. ## Who Needs to Take Action Most accounts migrate with no action required. You only need to take action if
your account uses any of the following: - A payment method added before 2024 that was never re-verified. - More than one billing contact on the account.
